text:
Evgeni Malkin has only ever played for one NHL team, and this week that became a live question. Darren Dreger reported that Malkin must submit a three-team trade list to the Penguins (as carried by Markerzone and HockeyFeed), and Dreger has linked him to Minnesota. It lands with Pittsburgh winless in four and a 40-year-old with three Stanley Cups being asked to name the places he'd go.

On the ice he still looks like someone a contender would want. He has 11 points in 14 games at about 17 minutes a night, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 10.6 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 96th percentile among forwards: the puck still finds a teammate in a good spot. Six goals on 4.0 expected (the quality of his chances) runs a little hot, and his last ten games came in under what we'd expect. Evolving-Hockey's read on 2025-26 is the honest scouting report: strong at creating chances, bottom 4% of forwards at preventing them. Whoever wants him is buying the offense and planning around the rest.
headline: Malkin's trade list, and what a buyer gets
